MARKET.head: Penfolds leads JD.com's Singles' Day wine rankings; Cloudy Bay and Tonhwa break in
MARKET.summ: China’s biggest online shopping season has produced a new set of winners in wine - and while familiar names dominate, a few less obvious brands have broken into the top 10
takeaways: Penfolds ranked first among wine brands on JD.com's Singles' Day rankings, ahead of Changyu and Great Wall.
Cloudy Bay, the New Zealand producer known for dry white, placed fifth, the only white-focused brand in the top 10.
JD.com did not disclose whether its rankings were based on sales value or volume, and alcohol transaction value rose 25% year over year.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting over 200 exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
India's free trade agreements with Australia, the UK and New Zealand, and January 2026 EU deal, are set to cut tariffs on some imported wines and spirits.
The event is organized by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice, with 12 national pavilions and over 1,000 brands.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine exports to China more than double in volume in Q3
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine exports to mainland China rose 1.9% by value in Q3 2026 while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China jumped 143.6% in the quarter, per Wine Australia data.
Mainland China remained Australia's largest wine export market by value, but nine-month export value there fell 10.4%.

MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH applies for bankruptcy liquidation amid falling prices
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai Free Trade Zone Wine Exchange Co., known as WINEXSH, applied for liquidation, reportedly reviewed by Shanghai Pudong court.
A Bordeaux supplier says WINEXSH left a latest en primeur order unpaid and uncollected, while consumers reported delayed collections and refunds.
Falling Chinese fine wine prices, with 2021-2022 futures now cheaper physically, left firms holding large inventories exposed.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell well at Shanghai consumer and trade festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival in Shanghai on November 7-8 drew nearly 600 consumers and about 300 trade professionals.
Exhibitors, including Ferngrove and Duke's Vineyard, reported on-site sales and importer interest that exceeded expectations.
Pran Wines' Hong Boyong said lesser-known 3 Drops drew distributor interest because of its value.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slipping as sales fall and mocktails rise
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: The essay asks whether wine is passé, drawing on Paul Krugman's 1987 essay asking whether free trade is passé.
Sales of wine and other alcoholic beverages have fallen dramatically, and restaurant tables often show fewer wine bottles.
The author compares wine to coffee, which has shifted from a default choice to one option among many.

CULTURE.head: James Halliday named 2026 Victorian Legend of the Vine by WCA
CULTURE.summ: Australian wine industry luminary James Halliday AM has been named the 2026 Victorian Legend of the Vine by Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA), in recognition of his “extraordinary contribution to the Australian wine industry spanning more than five decades”. Announced at the 2026 Melbourne Royal Wine Awards Trophy Lunch on...
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia named James Halliday AM the 2026 Victorian Legend of the Vine at the Melbourne Royal Wine Awards on 13 November.
Halliday has authored dozens of books since 1979 and created what WCA calls Australia's most trusted wine reference.
He is the tenth Victorian to receive the honour, and his son Angus accepted it on his behalf.

CULTURE.head: Pooley Syrah wins Jimmy Watson Trophy at 2026 Melbourne Royal Wine Awards
CULTURE.summ: The results of the 2026 Melbourne Royal Wine Awards have been revealed, with Pooley Wines taking home the coveted Jimmy Watson Memorial Trophy for its 2025 Pooley Syrah. The win marks a significant achievement for the Tasmanian producer, with the 2025 Pooley Syrah also awarded the Trevor Mast Trophy for Best Shiraz and Best...
takeaways: The same Syrah also took the Trevor Mast Trophy for Best Shiraz and Best Tasmanian Shiraz.
Oakridge Wines of Victoria's Yarra Valley won three trophies, including Best Pinot Noir for its 2025 864 Henk Aqueduct Block.

CULTURE.head: ASVO honours AWRI's Mark Krstic and Treasury's James Godfrey for industry service
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) celebrates the work of long-established wine career professionals. This year, AWRI’s Mark Krstic was honoured as the ASVO’s 31st ‘Fellow of the Society’ and Treasury Wine Estate’s James Godfrey was recognised through a newly created ‘Lifetime Acknowledgement Award’.
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology named AWRI managing director Dr Mark Krstic its 2026 Fellow of the Society.
Treasury Wine Estates winemaker James Godfrey received the society's new Lifetime Acknowledgement Award, mainly for his work with fortified wines.
Godfrey has announced his retirement, and Krstic's AWRI tenure is ending as he steps back from the managing director role.

CULTURE.head: Victorian Wine Show names Point Leo Estate's Chardonnay Best Wine of Show
CULTURE.summ: The trophy winners for the 46th Annual Victorian Wine Show (VWS) have been announced with a “healthy mix of emerging smaller wineries and seasoned campaigners celebrating success”. The judging took place in Nagambie over three intensive days, with a total of 612 entries from 124 wineries. The annual show “recognises excellence...
takeaways: The 46th Victorian Wine Show in Nagambie judged 612 entries from 124 wineries, awarding 21 trophies in total.
Point Leo Estate's 2024 Reserve Chardonnay took Best Wine of Show, while Pfeiffer Wines was named Most Successful Exhibitor.
Hirsch Hill's 2026 Garnacha Blanca, its first vintage of that variety, won Best Iberian Variety Wine.

CULTURE.head: VinePair host reflects on American wine in 2026 and ways to celebrate it
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of VinePair's podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026 in an episode.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace, with no specific wine data or numbers reported.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names 2026 Viticulturist and Winemaker of the Year and other award winners
CULTURE.summ: Last night, the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) revealed the winners of its Awards for Excellence. The ASVO said the winners were chosen from a very high calibre and diverse range of submissions showing expertise across winemaking, viticulture and wine science. Highlights of the evening included the naming...
takeaways: Chris Dent, owner of Gorton Drive Estate and chair of Murray Valley Winegrowers, was named 2026 Viticulturist of the Year by the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology.
David Bicknell, a winemaker of almost 25 years at Oakridge Wines, was named 2026 Winemaker of the Year.
Tracey Siebert of the Australian Wine Research Institute won the Wine Science and Technology Award, with around 2,800 citations across 48 indexed publications.

CULTURE.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water footprint threatens wine's green reputation
CULTURE.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wine sector has built its brand around sustainability, a claim consumers increasingly expect.
Industry's growing use of AI tools, from tasting posters to wine labels, is framed as a risk to consumer trust.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to read vineyard soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity (EC) mapping from 2021 to guide over 30 soil pits.
The maps revealed limestone density differences about 1.5 meters down that were hard to see from the surface.
For the 2026 vintage, trimmed Pinot Noir reached 14.5% potential alcohol, while tressed vines on denser limestone reached 13.6%.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its Agrochemical & MRL Search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google stores.
The free app gives rapid access to information in the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet, known as the Dog book.
Users with the app already installed are asked to perform an update so they keep receiving app updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/16/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais bulk prices fell in 2026: Mâcon-Villages Blanc down 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc down 13 per cent, despite higher bulk volumes.
Puligny-Montrachet's 2024 reference price was about €3,050 a hectolitre versus about €817 for Pouilly-Fuissé, close to four times higher.

NEWSLETTERS.head: An English wine harvest round-up, with four top producers, over lunch at Woven
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Woven by Adam Smith is a Michelin-starred restaurant at the Coworth Park hotel, near Ascot, Berkshire (UK). This was my
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Rathfinny's Mark Driver said 2026 vintage ran about three weeks earlier than normal, with his Pinot picked on 2 September.
Danbury Ridge's Jon Atkinson reported 1,427 growing degree days overall in 2026, versus 1,800 in Burgundy.
Hundred Hills' Stephen Duckett sells most wine directly through a wine club and uses no conventional marketing, relying on word-of-mouth referral.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Choosing Thanksgiving Wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: No single wine pairs perfectly with the Thanksgiving meal, but many styles can shine on your table
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker recommends keeping wines at or below 13% alcohol, preferably 12.5%, so diners stay alert at midday meals.
Champagne in any style is her classic sparkling pick, with Crémant, Método classico and Lambrusco offered as alternatives or bold choices.
Chardonnay and off-dry Riesling are named as traditional matches, with Etna Bianco from Carricante offered as a bold white pick.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, founded 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began Cabernet Franc with its 2019 vintage.
Forge makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from four different soils, including Willow, Railroad, Arlo and Bellows.
In 2023 Forge made its Cabernet Franc with no stems to study tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sixteen Austrian Wines You Should Try
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delicious recommendations,including old favourites and new discoveries
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Fischer's Sauvignon Blanc St. Anna 2025 is made by brothers Klaus and Bernard, who started making wine at the family business in 2015.
Franz Hofstätter's declassified Grüner Veltliner from the Achleiten vineyard in the Wachau is highlighted for its struck match and iodine aromas.
Hajszan Neumann's Grüner Veltliner Natural 2025 from Fritz Weininger's winery is priced at €15 from Lebendige Weine for the 2023 vintage.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics are judged by whether their expertise suits their audience, with the sweet spot being slightly above target readers' level.
Atkin says conflicts of interest are less concerning to him than undisclosed social ties, and cites research that disclosure can make advisors more self-interested.
Atkin's main criticism is that wine reviewers spend too little time assessing wines, often about 30 seconds per sample, and suggests readers fund reviewers they trust.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and private cellar sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or uploaded images, and Orpheus notifies them and connects them with sellers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish indigenous grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava takes its name from the cellars, or caves, dug to store the wine, and became a formal Spanish legal label term in 1972.
Sumarroca's 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, made from Macabeu, Xarel·lo and Parellada, was aged 40 months and costs $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop planned for November 6.
Per WBO stats, Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy and a quarter of Australia.
Reviewer singled out Piqueras' El Abuelo, a blend of Alicante Bouschet, Monastrell and Syrah, as a standout for its elegance and restrained oak.
